---
title: Production auto-publish reconciler
description: The read-only Cron Control job that flags stale auto-publish stop fences, leftover split or staged Worker deployments and Workers off the production SHA, with its credentials, bounds, deduplication and stop fence.
updatedAt: "2026-11-28"
---

The `production-auto-publish-reconcile` job in
[Cron Control](/build/devops/cloudflare-cron-control) checks, once an hour,
that automatic production publication has left nothing behind. It only
reads: it never dispatches a workflow, writes a GitHub variable, secret or
setting, or changes a Cloudflare Worker, version or deployment. It reports
through the shared root operator alert, the same path as SLO burn and cost
alerts ([observability](/build/devops/observability-analytics)).

The job is registered but **disabled**: it is not listed in
`CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS`. Admitting it is a staged transition (see
[Enable](#enable)) that needs the release owner's approval.

## What it flags

| Flag | Source | Condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stale stop fence | GitHub repository variables `PRODUCTION_AUTO_PUBLISH` and `PRODUCTION_AUTO_PUBLISH_<FAMILY>` | The value is `stopped` and its last update is older than the stop window (24 hours), or the value is `stopped:<ISO until>[:reason]` and `until` has passed |
| Leftover split | Cloudflare active deployment of each automatic Worker | The deployment holds more than one version, or one version below 100% (a 0% candidate stage counts), and was created longer ago than the split TTL (120 minutes) |
| Lagging Worker | Public `/api/build-info` of each automatic Worker against `refs/heads/production` | The build-info commit differs from the production SHA for longer than the lag window (120 minutes), counted from the first run that saw the ref at that SHA |

Any other fence value publishes, so only `stopped` and the `stopped:` form
are checked. The first sighting of each production SHA is kept as a single
pending-work item in the Cron Control ledger, so the lag window starts when
the ref moved rather than at the commit's own date. Credential expiry is not
checked here; the token rotation reminder owns it.

The automatic Workers are listed in
`apps/cron-control/src/processors/auto-publish-reconcile/catalog.ts`. They are
the serving Workers of `scripts/ci/serving-workers-apps.mjs`, read at each
app's first origin, and a test fails when the two lists differ. Admin and the
vinext families join when their own automatic publication lands.

Windows can be tuned with optional text bindings, each a whole number within
bounds; anything else keeps the default:
`AUTO_PUBLISH_RECONCILE_STOP_WINDOW_HOURS` (1 to 720),
`AUTO_PUBLISH_RECONCILE_SPLIT_TTL_MINUTES` and
`AUTO_PUBLISH_RECONCILE_LAG_WINDOW_MINUTES` (30 to 10,080).

## Credentials

Both are operator-installed Worker secrets, read by name and sent only to
their own provider. Neither appears in logs, alert text or alert data.

- `AUTO_PUBLISH_RECONCILE_CLOUDFLARE_TOKEN`: an account API token with
  **Workers Scripts Read** only, no zone permissions. It reads deployments;
  it cannot upload, stage, promote or roll back. The account comes from the
  existing `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` binding.
- `AUTO_PUBLISH_RECONCILE_GITHUB_TOKEN`: a fine-grained token for the
  `tutur3u/platform` repository only, with **Variables: read** and
  **Contents: read**. GitHub has no narrower grant for a named variable, so
  the token can read every repository variable value, which are not secrets,
  but cannot read secrets or write variables, refs or settings.

Each half runs on its own: without the GitHub token, only splits are checked;
without the Cloudflare token, only fences and lag. With neither, the run
fails without any request. The deploy coordinator holds no GitHub
credential, which is why this job lives in Cron Control.

## Bounds

| Bound | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Workers scanned | The catalog, at most 16 |
| Provider requests | 5 variable pages, 1 ref read, 1 deployments read and 1 build-info read per Worker: at most 39, enforced by a request budget |
| Alerts | At most one RPC per run |
| Wall time | 60 seconds, inside the 90-second processor deadline of its 120-second lease |
| Per request | 15 seconds, 1 MiB body, redirects refused |
| Retries | None in a run; the next hourly slot is the retry |

A variable listing longer than five pages fails the run instead of paging on,
so a fence is never missed silently. A refused, rate-limited or timed-out
Cloudflare read ends that run's Cloudflare reads.

## Deduplication and outcomes

An alert's dedupe key is
`auto-publish:reconcile:<32 hex of SHA-256 over the sorted finding ids>`.
Each id names its fact: the variable and its update time, the Worker and its
deployment id, or the Worker with its live and production SHAs. The same
state on later slots reuses the key, and `private.send_root_operator_alert`
answers `null` without notifying anyone. A new fact makes a new key and one
new alert. A clean state sends nothing.

| Outcome | When |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` | Every configured source was read; an alert, if any, was delivered or was already sent |
| `degraded` | A half is unconfigured, a build-info read failed, or the alert found no recipient (the key is released, so the next slot delivers it) |
| `failed` | A GitHub or Cloudflare API read failed, no credential is set, or the alert RPC failed; no alert is sent for a partial read |
| `unknown` | The alert RPC answer was unreadable |
| `stopped` | The job's durable stop was seen |

Five consecutive failed slots exhaust the job's failure budget and stop it,
like any Cron Control job.

## Stop and resume

The job checks its durable ledger stop before the GitHub reads, before the
production ref read, before each Worker and before the alert. The operator
stop needs no deploy:

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CRON_CONTROL_OPERATOR_TOKEN" \
  https://<cron-control-host>/control/jobs/production-auto-publish-reconcile/stop
```

A stopped job claims no slot and makes no request. `resume` lifts the stop.
Removing the id from `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS` disables it in the next
publication.

## Enable

1. Install both secrets on `tuturuuu-cron-control` with the permissions above.
2. In one reviewed change, add `production-auto-publish-reconcile` to
   `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS` in `apps/cron-control/cloudflare.config.ts`,
   update `scripts/ci/fixtures/cf-worker-parity/cron-control.json` (the
   serving identity becomes `previousIdentity`, the new list `identity`) with
   a `transition.decision` that names the job, and update the registration
   test in `apps/cron-control/src/auto-publish-reconcile.test.ts`, which
   fails while the job is listed. The trigger set does not change: the job
   runs at minute 0 of the existing `*/30 * * * *` trigger.
3. Publish Cron Control through its workflow after the release owner's
   approval, then confirm the first hourly slot in `GET /control/jobs`.

## Cost envelope

At 24 slots a day a run makes at most 39 reads of the GitHub and Cloudflare
APIs (not billed per call), at most one database RPC and about 15 ledger
calls. The six build-info reads are Worker requests on the serving Workers:
144 a day. `apps/cron-control/src/auto-publish-reconcile.test.ts` counts
calls through the healthy, flagged, repeated, stopped, failing, restarted,
paged and slow cases.
